The brief

Make collaboration
the central idea.

Handshake brings coding agents together around a body of work. The identity should express that partnership; the interface should make it understandable.

Twine shares its name with established software projects. Handshake gives this product a new identity centered on the relationship between a person directing work and a machine helping carry it out.

The design starts with the familiar handshake emoji and gives its two hands different characters. The challenge is to carry that expression into a dense working tool while keeping tasks, responsibilities, and progress clear.

Why change the name

Twine has competing associations.

Existing GitHub projects already use Twine for publishing, translation, and interactive fiction. These are concrete reasons to establish a separate product identity.

  • pypa/twine ↗Python package publishing
  • scelis/twine ↗Translation management
  • klembot/twinejs ↗Interactive-fiction authoring

Why Handshake: it is available for the intended project namespace and directly describes human–machine collaboration. The name also has existing software uses, including an AI-agent credential tool; availability here is specific to this project.

01 / COLLABORATION

Make responsibility legible.

Stable roles, labeled states, and trace steps explain how agents contribute to the same task.

02 / CONCENTRATION

Keep attention on the work.

Quiet surfaces frame the terminal. Color identifies meaningful actions and states without competing with output.

03 / FAMILIARITY

Feel at home on the Mac.

System typography, native controls, and familiar keyboard behavior make the working environment dependable.

Identity guidelines

Wordmark and lockup

Write Handshake as one word in title case. Pair the detailed symbol with compact system sans-serif at weight 600 and −0.045 em tracking. Align the pair by optical center. At the minimum horizontal lockup, use a 48 pt symbol placement, 12 pt gap, and 30 pt wordmark.

Placement and clear space

Use the transparent symbol for lockups and quiet editorial grounds, a rounded tile for contained identity placements, a circular version for avatars, and a full-bleed square where a platform applies its own mask. Keep one eighth of the placement canvas clear on every outside edge.

Size and reproduction

The minimum standalone editorial placement is 48 pt. Below that size, evaluate the clasp and the separation between the hands at actual size. Resolve a simpler optical drawing for 16–32 px if needed. Final wordmark artwork should use outlined type for consistent reproduction.

Usage

Scale the complete artwork proportionally. Keep the clasp intact and retain the prism/brass relationship. Avoid stretching, recoloring hands for status, adding glow, or placing the transparent symbol over complex imagery. Monochrome adaptations need deliberate separation of overlapping forms.

Platform application

Review the macOS icon in Finder, Dock, app switcher, and About at actual sizes. Use the square artwork for platform-specific icon composition. The small-size drawing, final typography, and platform icon treatment are the next identity refinements.

Color, motion, and accessibility guidelines

Color roles

Charcoal and ivory establish the identity grounds. Brass identifies primary actions. Prism color belongs to the symbol. Blue identifies implementer, orange reviewer, purple coordinator, and green worker. Keep role, operational state, selection, and focus independent.

Motion

Use 120 ms for hover, 180 ms for selection, 200 ms for disclosure, and 220 ms for inspector transitions. Movement should explain a direct action. Reduced motion removes movement and animation durations.

Accessibility

Use 4.5:1 as the minimum ordinary-text contrast and 3:1 for meaningful non-text boundaries and indicators. Status includes a label and icon. Keep focus visible alongside selection, support app zoom, and provide full names when visible labels truncate. Use opaque fills with reduced transparency and stronger boundaries with increased contrast.

Review native keyboard behavior, VoiceOver, inactive windows, and real materials in complete product flows. User-selected terminal palettes need their own contrast review.

Component behavior and content

Actions and forms

Use verb-led labels and persistent field labels. Preserve button width and label while busy; prevent duplicate submission. Validate on submission or after an edited field loses focus. Place errors beside the field and clear them when corrected. Enter submits a valid form; Escape cancels its sheet. Icon-only controls need an accessible name and help text.

Navigation

A folder anchors the sidebar, with files and sessions in separate sections. Selecting a session opens its work without launching a workflow. Selection persists when focus moves elsewhere. Context menus act on the clicked row. Long names truncate with the full name available through help and accessibility text.

Workflow and agent tabs

A workflow occupies a top-level tab. Its symbol, name, status, and close action remain distinguishable. Show close actions on hover and keyboard focus without shifting the title. In Tabs, agent selection changes the visible terminal. In Bento, pane headers identify each agent and a focus outline identifies the pane receiving input.

Terminal and traces

Keep the terminal's input, rendering, selection, and copy/paste behavior intact. Individual mode appears in both layouts and starts no work when toggled. Trace Overview uses shared start order; In Depth uses observed time. Selecting a span opens contextual detail. Escape closes its inspector and returns focus to the source.

Content resilience

Check long names, many tabs, empty traces, busy and disabled actions, multi-line errors, and inactive windows in both appearances. Errors identify the affected item and a useful next action. Retain loaded content when a recoverable read fails.

P.01 / WORKING HIERARCHY

The terminal stays primary.

Brand expression lives in the identity and chrome. Terminal colors and typography remain under the user’s control.

P.02 / INDEPENDENT STATES

Selection, role, and focus.

Selected tabs orient. Stable role colors identify responsibility. The focus ring tells you where keyboard input goes.

P.03 / EXPLAIN THE PAST

History has a clear boundary.

A restored transcript is labeled. Traces explain the sequence without suggesting that old output is a running process.

Product scenarios and language

Working hierarchy

A folder contains sessions; a session contains workflows; a workflow coordinates agents through roles. The welcome screen introduces Handshake and offers Open folder. Once a folder opens, its name becomes the window's orientation anchor.

Attention and return to work

Pair a needs-attention state with a contextual explanation. Distinguish an input request, a recoverable failure, and a stopped process. Label restored output as a transcript from a process that is no longer running; resumption remains explicit.

Constrained layouts

Preserve useful terminal height before allocating space to secondary information. Reflow toolbar actions as width or zoom increases pressure on the layout. Trace bodies scroll independently. Use a constrained inspector or sheet when side-by-side detail becomes unreadable.

Terminology

Use folder for the user's directory, session for a body of work, workflow for its top-level tab, role for responsibility, harness for the external tool, and agent for the process filling a role. Use direct actions such as Open folder, New session, Resume agent, and Show traces.

Design review & rollout

Evaluate the identity
in the whole product.

Review recognition, working hierarchy,
and consistency across touchpoints.

01 / RECOGNITION

Does the gesture hold at small sizes?

Compare the clasp at 16–32 px with larger placements. Resolve where a simpler optical drawing is needed.

02 / BALANCE

Does the wordmark support the symbol?

Evaluate letterforms, weight, spacing, and scale together on ivory and charcoal.

03 / HIERARCHY

Does the work stay in focus?

Compare active work, attention, and trace detail. Check that identity, action, and state each have the right emphasis.

Carry the name across the experience.
